subject: Unable to include ggvis in a for loop

messages.author: c041c5f617641723
messages.subject: Unable to include ggvis in a for loop
parts:
Not sure if this is the right place to post this, or knitr/rmarkdown will be a better choice, but here is the issue:

I want to print multiple ggvis plot in a loop:
```{r, results='asis'}
library(ggvis)
library(knitr)
for(i in 1:5)
  ggvis(mtcars, ~cyl, ~mpg) %>% layer_points()
```

I tried surrounding the statement with print, changing results to different values, and using *apply instead. Nothing has worked so far.

If I use lapply and assign the result to plots, for example. Then I'm able to print plots with:
```{r}
plots[[1]]
plots[[2]]
plots[[3]]
```

Thanks ahead for any advice or suggestions!

messages.author: c041c5f617641723
messages.subject: Re: Unable to include ggvis in a for loop
parts:
Tried that too. didn't work :(

So here's my ugly workaround:

plots <- lapply(1:5, function(x){
  ggvis(mtcars, ~cyl, ~mpg) %>% layer_points() %>% knit_print
})
html <- paste0(lapply(plots, unclass), collapse = "\n")
asis_output(html, ggvis_dependencies(absolute = TRUE, in_shiny = FALSE))
```

So the issue seems to be that the internal `knit_print` implementation in `ggvis` outputs a `asis` output. However, knitr couldn't understand when such output wrapped inside a for-loop. So I extracted the raw html and collapsed them into one. Glue it with ggvis dependencies for meta. That worked for me.

Not sure if we can fix this in `ggvis` or this is some work for `knitr` instead.

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Unable to include ggvis in a for loop
parts:
Sorry I do not have a better solution than the hack... Shiny tags have
the same problem, and hers are shiny's knit_print methods:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/a0df8f349/R/app.R#L280-L300
Basically the methods will collect dependencies, and render the tags
recursively to obtain the HTML code. That is how multiple tags /
inputs embedded in another tag will still work. Perhaps ggvis can have
something similar (like ggvis_multiple(a_list_of_ggvis_objects)), and
you have provided the prototype.

Regards,
Yihui
